description_full: Green Brick Partners, Inc. operates as a diversified homebuilding and land development company in the United States. The company engages in the homebuilding process, which includes acquiring and developing land, securing entitlements, designing homes, constructing properties, providing title, mortgage, and insurance agency services, and managing marketing and sales, as well as creating master-planned communities. It also provides financial services platforms, including Green Brick Title, GRBK Mortgage, and Green Brick Insurance. Green Brick Partners, Inc. was incorporated in 2006 and is headquartered in Plano, Texas.
ceo_bio: Mr. James R. Brickman | Co-Founder, Co-CEO & Director | Age 73 | Compensation: $5.0M (FY2024)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 620 people. Revenue per employee of $3.4M ranks in the top quartile among Consumer Cyclical peers, with revenue growing 9%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $336K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $20K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 1× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (2/10).
financial_summary: Green Brick Partners, Inc. is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $2.6B market cap on $2.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years and +22% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 20% against a 10% cost of capital — a 10-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 23% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $208M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.68×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.7× net debt/EBITDA.

Shareholder yield of 3.3% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 8.5% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
